newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Midday Update.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Midday Update.

text.p: HOWARD AND CLINTON DISCUSS GOLF
Prime Minister, John Howard, and U-S President, Bill Clinton, started their meeting in Canberra by discussing one of the President's favourite subjects - golf.
Mr Clinton says he's willing to back Australia's bid to have the President's Cup tournament held in Australia in 1998, a move Mr Howard says would delight him.
But the two men got down to more serious talks soon after.
The talks have now ended, having run 30 minutes over their allotted 60 minutes.
The two met by themselves for 20 minutes, before being joined by three officials from each country.
They are now meeting with the Cabinet

On a light-hearted note, Mr Clinton has rejected suggestions he brought a golf-pro to Australia with him, although says he'll need all the help he can get in a game tomorrow against Greg Norman, the world's top golfer.
BRYANT HEARING TOLD OF HELICOPTER DEMAND
A Hobart court has been told Port Arthur gunman Martin Bryant asked for a helicopter to take him to Hobart Airport after being surrounded by police at the Seascape Guest House on April 28.
The Crown says Bryant demanded he be flown to Adelaide with one of three hostages he'd been holding.
The Crown says Bryant told a police negotiator he wanted to take Noelene Martin with him and release her husband David, and hostage Glen Pears.
However Crown Counsel Nick Perks said the three were probably already dead...their bodies recovered some time later from the burnt out guest house.
The hearing is continuing.
CLINTON LAYS A WREATH
United States President, Bill Clinton, has mixed with onlookers in Canberra after performing the first official duty of his trip to Australia.
The President and his wife, Hillary, shook hands with members of the crowd, and agreed to sign autographs for a small group of children.
Earlier, Mr Clinton had placed a wreath at the tomb of the unknown soldier at the National War Memorial in Canberra.
The Clintons were accompanied by Prime Minister, John Howard, and his wife, and Veterans' Affairs Minister, Bruce Scott.
After placing the wreath, Mr Clinton inspected the names of Australian soldiers who died in battle.
From the memorial's balcony, Mr Scott pointed out the sights of Canberra to the Clintons, including Parliament House.
SOME DISAPPOINTMENT IN CLINTON VISIT
Federal Opposition leader Kim Beazley has expressed some regret about aspects of the Clintons' Australian visit.
Mr Beazley, who'll have a 20 minute meeting with the US President this afternoon, says he'll be raising trade disputes between Australia and the United States in the talks.
But he says he's disappointed television coverage of the meeting hasn't been allowed.
And he's also expressed concern female representatives from some sides of politics appear not to have been invited to a meeting with Mrs Clinton.
CLAIMS HILLARY IS SNUBBING NON-COALITION FEMALE MPs
Democrats' Senator, Natasha Stott-Despoja, says she's disappointed no women politicians outside the Coalition have been invited to hold discussions with Hillary Clinton.
The American First Lady has asked for a private meeting to be organised with Australian women who represent areas in which she's interested.
At this stage, no Democrats or Federal Labor Party women have been invited to the meeting.
Senator Stott-Despoja says it's disappointing because for many women from all sides of politics, Mrs Clinton is a role-model.
BABYSITTER FOUND NOT GUILTY OF MURDER
A 35-year-old Sydney woman has been found not guilty of murdering an 18-month-old girl she was babysitting.
A short time ago a Supreme Court jury returned its verdict in the trial of Linda Margaret Funk of Maroubra after deliberating for more than 24-hours.
The jury also found Mrs Funk not guilty of manslaughter.
Elspeth Lawson died of massive head injuries in November 1992.
The defence had claimed Mrs Funk accidently dropped the child after she'd thrown her into the air.
INITIAL FINDINGS INTO MINE DISASTER EXPECTED
New South Wales Mines Minister, Bob Martin, says he expects to get a preliminary report on Newcastle's Gretley mine disaster as early as next week.
Funerals are being held today for the four men who lost their lives last week.
Mr Martin says work won't be resuming until tomorrow as a mark of respect to the dead.
MINERS' FUNERALS HELD TODAY
The funerals of the four Gretley Colliery miners killed in last week's accident in Wallsend, New South Wales, are being held today.
Mark Kaiser, John Hunter, Damon Murray and Edward Batterham, died last week when the section of tunnel they were working in flooded with water.
Mine owners Oakbridge say as a mark of respect to the four men, the mine will remain closed until tomorrow.
Meanwhile, investigations into the accident by the company, the miners' union and the State Government are underway.
IR CHANGES "A BAD DAY FOR WORKERS"
The Federal Opposition says the Senate's passing of the Government's industrial relations reforms marks a bad day for nine million Australian workers.
The Senate last night passed the Workplace Relations Bill after a marathon debate.
The Government says the changes will help business, encourage job creation and protect the disadvantaged.
But Shadow Industrial Relations Minister, Bob McMullan, says the legislation breaks the Government's promise that no worker would be worse off under the new system.
NSW COPS BIG HEALTH FUNDING REDUCTION
Federal Health Minister, Michael Wooldridge, says New South Wales deserves the biggest share of cuts to the states' health budgets because it's been "rorting the system".
State Health Minister, Andrew Refshauge, confirmed this morning that New South Wales would lose 34 million dollars in Federal health funding, taking the biggest cut of all the states.
Dr Wooldridge told ABC Radio that New South Wales is being penalised for shifting its public health costs onto the Medicare system more than any other state.
NTH QLD PRISONER DIES
A prisoner from the Townsville jail, in north Queensland, has died in hospital after being found hanging in his cell yesterday afternoon.
The 39-year-old man was taken to the Townsville General Hospital late yesterday afternoon.
His condition remained critical throughout the night, and he died about an hour ago.
Prison General Manager, John McGowan, says his name hasn't been released as relatives are still being informed.
Officers from the Corrective Services Investigation Unit are on their way to Townsville.
TIGER-MANIA TAKES SPOTLIGHT FROM SHARK
The entry of 20 year old golf prodigy, Tiger Woods, in this year's Australian Open has taken the spotlight away from world number one, Greg Norman.
Norman is four to one favourite for the event, but says this year's tournament will be different for him, because for once, all eyes are on someone else.
Norman says the hype surrounding Woods, who only turned professional in September but has already won one event, hasn't been seen at the Australian Open before.
He says even when some of golf's contemporary greats, like Seve Ballesteros and Nick Faldo, played in the tournament, there wasn't the same sort of mania.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
